summary: Flow-control cascade in eu-west causing request replay loop, streaming stalls, and enterprise escalation (AstralTech)
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC and 2026-03-10 05:10 UTC AstralTech experienced a production incident in eu-west where a flow-control regression triggered a cascade of retries and request replays across the serving runtime. Symptoms included repeated partial streaming responses, stalled streams, and an anomalous billing uptick due to duplicate token charges. The customer escalated to enterprise SRE and Legal due to user-visible duplicate completions in chat workflows.

Impact: ~12% of AstralTech prod traffic in eu-west saw >=1 repeated completion; median tail latency for streaming requests increased from 180ms to 2.4s during the window. Streaming connections intermittently stalled (clients observing 'stream reset' or truncated final chunks). No data corruption reported, but there were repeated token billing events for the same logical request that generated an invoice spike.
timeline: 2026-03-10 03:36 UTC: AstralTech support alert via support phone + email reporting intermittent truncated streams.
2026-03-10 03:40 UTC: Automated alert: api-gateway observed a 7x increase in upstream 5xx-to-4xx error ratio for eu-west streaming endpoints.
2026-03-10 03:45 UTC: Support triage call — routed to SRE and runtime on-call (Marco Chen). Customer assigned P0 escalation.
2026-03-10 04:05 UTC: Engineering identified autoscaler thrashing events and brokered a temporary increase of burst capacity for AstralTech pool.
2026-03-10 04:22 UTC: Hotfix deployed to pin request-retry timeout to 6s (was 2s in recent rollout), which reduced repeat-request incidence.
2026-03-10 04:40 UTC: Streaming stability improved; customer confirmed fewer truncated responses but reported a small set of persistent request replays.
2026-03-10 05:10 UTC: Traffic normalized after autoscaler tuning and kernel selection rollback for a new quantized variant.
2026-03-13 10:00 UTC: Post-incident follow-up meeting; agreed remediation and billing credit plan with AstralTech.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send high-throughput concurrent streaming completion requests pinned to redwood/gpt-4o-infer-v1 in eu-west.
2) Simulate connection churn by repeatedly opening and closing streaming clients with short-lived TLS sessions.
3) Observe autoscaler scaling events on the customer-specific GPU pool and watch for repeated replayed requests in request logs (same request-id with multiple completion tokens).
logs_and_diagnostics: api-gateway logs: elevated upstream reset_by_peer and 502 errors from serving-runtime during scale-up windows (03:40-04:10 UTC).
serving-runtime: KV-cache eviction spikes coinciding with new quantized kernel rollout (commit 9b3c2f).
autoscaler: rapid scale-out then immediate scale-in cycles for astraltech-eu-west pool; metrics show high variance in active pods per minute.
billing: duplicate token invoicing patterns for identical request-ids (correlated with replay events).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis centered on the recent quantized-kernel rollout (9b3c2f) which decreased per-instance memory headroom and increased KV eviction rates. Elevated eviction caused longer cold-start latencies for resumed streams, which triggered client-side retry behavior; retries were occasionally honored as new requests due to an earlier change to request-id reconciliation in api-gateway (recent PR altered request dedup window). The interaction between shorter retry timeouts (2s), autoscaler cooldowns, and the kernel memory regression created a window where multiple retry attempts overlapped with partial completions — resulting in duplicate billing and truncated streams.

Key findings: (1) Kernel rollout reduced effective serving capacity for streaming traffic under high churn. (2) Gateway dedup window inadvertently shortened in a concurrent patch, allowing some retries to be treated as new requests. (3) Autoscaler cooldown parameters amplified oscillation under bursty churn.
actions_taken:
Immediate: rolled back quantized kernel (reverted commit 9b3c2f) for astraltech pool, increased request deduplication window to 30s in api-gateway config for streaming endpoints, and temporarily increased burst capacity for the customer's dedicated pool. Tuned autoscaler cooldowns to avoid immediate scale-in after scale-out.

Customer comms: Provided hourly status updates during incident, arranged an executive-resolution call within the hour of escalation, and committed to a billing credit for duplicate token charges.

Followed up: Created INT-4310 to track autoscaler policy review and linked a PR to add end-to-end request-id dedup tests for streaming flows.
resolution: Incident mitigated by rolling back the quantized kernel rollout for AstralTech's eu-west pool and adjusting gateway dedup and autoscaler parameters. Streaming stability and duplicate-charge patterns returned to baseline by 2026-03-10 05:10 UTC. Customer billing credit agreed and scheduled; postmortem meeting held on 2026-03-13.
root_cause: A three-way interaction: (1) a recently deployed quantized kernel variant increased KV cache churn and reduced memory headroom, (2) a concurrent api-gateway change shortened the request deduplication window, and (3) autoscaler cooldowns permitted oscillation under connection churn. These combined to allow retries to be accepted as new requests during partial completion windows, resulting in duplicate completions and streaming truncation.
follow_up_actions: 1) Autoscaler policy rewrite (INT-4310) — target: smoother scale transitions for customer-dedicated pools (owner: infra-team, ETA: 2026-04-02).
2) Add streaming integration tests that exercise request-id dedup under churn and validate billing dedup logic (owner: runtime-qe, ETA: 2026-03-24).
3) Harden rollback gating for kernel variants: require end-to-end streaming perf test pass before rollout to dedicated pools (owner: model-onboarding, ETA: 2026-04-09).
4) Customer remediation: issue billing credit for duplicate token charges and provide a runbook for safe retry parameters (owner: CS-Billing, ETA: 2026-03-18).
5) Schedule a customer readout and technical deep-dive with AstralTech (owner: Solutions, date: 2026-03-20).
